title: Mutual E2EE synchronization and enrichment of participant speech transcripts and training evidence
goal: Extend personalized semantic speech so both participants compare their independently produced transcripts, alignments, correction observations and consented training evidence, resolve differences deterministically and enrich each participant-local dataset without blindly copying raw audio, transcripts or model state. Each side retains ownership, provenance, consent and deletion control over its contributions.

codebase_alignment.voice_contract: voice_runtime/schemas.py already provides transcript candidates, words, segments, confidence, disagreement_regions, decision_trace and provenance; synchronization must exchange compatible derived evidence rather than introduce an unrelated transcript model.
codebase_alignment.semantic_speech_parent: todos/todo.ai-snake-personalized-semantic-speech-stream.json already defines speech_training_evidence.v1, pair-scoped consent, transcript/source alignment, ML-Intern curation, evaluation and pair-scoped adapters.
codebase_alignment.pair_transport: docs/architecture/pair-view-sync.md and the semantic WebRTC parent todo provide E2EE DataChannel transport, opaque Hub relay fallback, epochs, replay protection, task leases and validators.
codebase_alignment.ml_intern: ML-Intern already supports immutable content-addressed datasets, deterministic splitting, validation, isolated training, evaluation, approval and rollback. Peer synchronization must terminate in curated immutable manifests, not mutable shared training folders.
codebase_alignment.constraint: Current ML-Intern intentionally does not automatically ingest voice usage. Peer exchange therefore requires explicit bilateral consent, quality admission and an authenticated curation mutation.

principles: Each participant independently transcribes and evaluates the same utterance whenever compute permits.
Differences are useful supervision signals and must be preserved as alternatives until resolved.
No last-writer-wins merge for transcripts, timestamps, speaker identity or consent.
Raw audio remains local by default; peers exchange hashes, bounded features, alignments, candidate text and quality evidence unless raw-audio sharing is separately granted.
Every imported contribution retains contributor, source session, model, revision, digest, quality and consent provenance.
A participant may accept, reject, quarantine or locally redact each received evidence group.
Dataset enrichment is directional: A may learn from B without requiring B to import A's evidence.
Revocation propagates through evidence references, curated manifests, queued jobs, active adapters and caches according to policy.
AI-Snake explains and proposes merges; deterministic validation and participant consent decide them.

sync_modes.transcript_consensus: Exchange candidate transcripts, word timings, confidence and disagreement regions; compute a shared resolution while retaining both originals.
sync_modes.evidence_enrichment: Exchange consented quality-approved training evidence descriptors and optionally encrypted content chunks so each peer may extend its own immutable dataset.
sync_modes.federated_update_exchange: Optional later mode exchanging bounded adapter updates or gradients instead of examples; disabled until poisoning, privacy and aggregation controls are proven.

tasks.title: Define bilateral evidence ownership, consent and revocation semantics
tasks.description: Specify who owns captured audio, local transcript candidates, corrections, derived features, imported evidence and trained adapters. Define asymmetric consent and post-revocation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Capture consent, transcript sharing, feature sharing, raw-audio sharing, dataset import, training and adapter export are independent grants.
Each evidence field records its contributor and lawful/contractual purpose scope.
A recipient cannot widen purpose, retention or trainer location during import.
Revocation defines actions for ephemeral buffers, immutable manifests, queued/running jobs, approved adapters, exported copies and audit tombstones.
Neither participant can silently enroll the other participant's voice into unrelated models.
Hub/SFU remains unable to inspect plaintext in strict-E2EE mode.

tasks.title: Create strict schemas for inventory, diff, offer, resolution, receipt and revocation
tasks.description: Version and bound all peer evidence synchronization messages with epochs, sequences, hashes, expiry, signatures and explicit content scopes.
acceptance_criteria: Schemas reject oversized text, word arrays, feature vectors, group lists and unknown security-sensitive properties.
Inventory and diff use content identifiers without exposing private local paths.
Offer identifies exact fields and whether encrypted content chunks are included.
Resolution retains original candidate references and unresolved regions.
Receipts are signed by recipients and cannot be interpreted as broader consent.
Python and TypeScript validators pass shared valid, tampered, stale, replayed and oversized fixtures.

tasks.title: Build content-addressed utterance and evidence-group identity
tasks.description: Create stable privacy-aware identifiers that let peers recognize evidence for the same utterance without relying on filenames or mutable transcript text.
acceptance_criteria: Identity binds session epoch, speaker scope, time range and source digest or consented privacy-preserving fingerprint.
Transcript revisions do not create unrelated utterance identities.
Different utterances are not merged merely because normalized text matches.
Identifier generation is deterministic and versioned.
Cross-session correlation is disabled unless explicitly required by the consented training scope.
Collision and privacy tests cover repeated phrases, silence, clipped segments and reconnect epochs.

tasks.title: Implement independent transcript-candidate comparison and conflict graph
tasks.description: Compare candidates from speaker and listener ASR pipelines at word and timing level. Produce a conflict graph instead of flattening disagreements.
acceptance_criteria: Exact agreement, punctuation-only difference, lexical conflict, timing conflict, insertion, deletion, uncertain region and speaker-overlap are distinct states.
Candidate model, confidence, provenance and revision remain available after resolution.
Consensus cannot invent a word absent from every candidate or authoritative delayed source evidence.
Low-confidence agreement is not treated as independently validated agreement.
Late higher-quality revisions can supersede resolution through a new monotonic revision.
Fixtures cover accents, homophones, names, code terms, numbers, interruptions and overlapping speech.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic transcript-resolution policy with peer validation
tasks.description: Resolve candidate differences using delayed source alignment, independent model evidence, glossary constraints and validator votes. AI-Snake may explain choices but cannot decide authoritatively.
acceptance_criteria: Identical ordered inputs yield identical resolution and reason codes.
Source-aligned final transcript outranks provisional candidates only when integrity and alignment checks pass.
Unresolved conflicts remain excluded or quarantined rather than guessed.
Self-reported confidence is weighted by observed model calibration and provenance validity.
A participant may locally override display text without rewriting shared training evidence provenance.
Every resolution can be reproduced from signed candidate references and policy version.

tasks.title: Add E2EE inventory and Merkle-diff synchronization
tasks.description: Exchange compact evidence inventories and request only missing or changed groups through the existing prioritized DataChannel and opaque relay fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Initial sync compares manifest roots before sending per-item metadata.
Diff requests reveal only identifiers permitted by current consent.
Messages are replay-protected, signed, expiry-bound, rate-limited and chunked with backpressure.
Interrupted transfers resume idempotently without duplicating evidence.
Transcript/control traffic has priority over bulk evidence transfer.
Standard audio and live transcript operation continue when synchronization is paused or fails.

tasks.title: Create directional evidence transfer and local admission pipeline
tasks.description: Allow each recipient to independently accept, reject, redact or quarantine evidence offered by the other participant.
acceptance_criteria: Import requires valid bilateral offer signatures and recipient acceptance.
Recipient revalidates consent, digests, schema, provenance, quality, alignment, speaker scope and retention locally.
Received candidate text never silently replaces locally captured evidence.
Duplicate and near-duplicate groups are merged by references while preserving both provenances.
Rejected and quarantined groups emit content-free reason codes.
A signed receipt reports accepted, rejected and quarantined identifiers without exposing local storage paths.

tasks.title: Extend immutable ML-Intern speech manifests with multi-contributor lineage
tasks.description: Build a new immutable dataset version when peer evidence is accepted. Preserve contributor-specific consent and provenance at record and field level.
acceptance_criteria: Existing dataset artifacts are never mutated in place.
New manifest references parent manifest and accepted enrichment receipts.
Each record distinguishes local capture, peer transcript candidate, peer correction, shared resolution and optional peer audio source.
Train/validation grouping prevents the same utterance or shared source from crossing partitions through different contributors.
A contributor's revoked evidence can be identified transitively in all descendant manifests.
Dataset preview redacts identities, transcripts and audio according to existing and new privacy policy.

tasks.title: Add poisoning, collusion and false-correction defenses
tasks.description: Prevent a malicious or malfunctioning peer from degrading transcripts, training evidence or adapters through fabricated confidence, altered text, replayed audio or targeted poisoning.
acceptance_criteria: Peer-provided confidence is calibrated separately from local confidence.
Digest mismatch, invalid provenance, repeated contradictory corrections and abnormal evidence distributions trigger quarantine.
No single peer candidate is considered independent multi-model agreement when models or source audio are shared.
Evaluation compares local-only, peer-enriched and generic baselines on held-out sessions.
Adapter activation fails on increased lexical hallucination, targeted phrase errors or cross-speaker leakage.
Security tests cover malicious speaker, malicious listener, compromised model and colluding validator scenarios.

tasks.title: Implement transitive revocation and dataset/model impact analysis
tasks.description: Trace revoked contributions through evidence groups, dataset versions, training jobs, evaluation reports and active adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Impact report identifies all directly and transitively affected artifacts by digest.
Queued jobs are cancelled and running jobs fenced before publishing affected artifacts.
Affected active adapters are unloaded or blocked according to consent policy.
Retraining from a clean parent manifest is proposed but never automatically approved.
Audit keeps content-free tombstones sufficient to reject replayed revoked evidence.
Peer receives a signed revocation acknowledgement or a bounded unresolved-delivery status.

tasks.title: Add Pair-Dev and AI-Snake evidence comparison UI
tasks.description: Show transcript differences, confidence/provenance, requested evidence fields, local admission decisions and dataset enrichment impact in understandable form.
acceptance_criteria: Users see both original candidates and the proposed shared resolution.
Unresolved words and timing conflicts are visible rather than silently hidden.
Consent screen names exact data fields, direction, purpose, retention and trainer locations.
Bulk accept is unavailable for raw audio, identity features, export or unresolved conflicts without explicit confirmation.
AI-Snake explains why evidence was accepted, rejected or quarantined using deterministic reason codes.
Users can pause sync, revoke sharing and remove uncurated received evidence immediately.

tasks.title: Benchmark mutual enrichment quality, cost and synchronization bandwidth
tasks.description: Measure whether exchanging independent transcripts and evidence improves models compared with local-only training, including synchronization overhead and harmful-data rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Compare generic, local-only, peer-enriched and blindly-merged baselines.
Report lexical accuracy, alignment, intelligibility, speaker similarity, correction rate, poisoning resistance and calibration.
Report inventory, diff, transcript, feature, optional audio and retransmission bytes separately.
Use held-out conversations, unseen phrases, names, accents, noise and overlapping speech.
Measure asymmetric cases where only one participant has strong ASR or training compute.
Release requires peer enrichment to beat local-only on declared metrics without privacy, hallucination or leakage regression.

definition_of_done: Two participants can independently transcribe the same speech and exchange signed candidate evidence over strict E2EE transport.
Transcript differences produce a reproducible conflict graph and deterministic resolution without deleting original candidates.
Each side can directionally accept, reject, redact or quarantine the other's offered evidence.
Accepted contributions create a new immutable ML-Intern speech dataset version with complete multi-contributor lineage.
Consent and revocation remain enforceable through dataset, job, adapter and cache lifecycle.
Poisoning and false-correction tests prevent blind mutual degradation.
AI-Snake explains proposals and conflicts but cannot grant consent, resolve authoritative text or activate adapters by itself.
Benchmarks demonstrate whether mutual enrichment provides measurable benefit over local-only learning.
